questions.stem: What is the basic structure of a mitochondrion?

options.text: A double membrane with the inner membrane folded into cristae, enclosing the matrix

questions.explanation: Mitochondria have a double membrane. The outer membrane is smooth, while the inner membrane is folded into cristae. The space inside is called the matrix.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the cristae in mitochondria?

options.text: To increase the surface area for the reactions of aerobic respiration

questions.explanation: The cristae (folds of the inner membrane) greatly increase the surface area available for the enzymes and electron carriers involved in the later stages of aerobic respiration, maximising ATP production.

questions.stem: What is the matrix of a mitochondrion?

options.text: The space between the two membranes
The fluid-filled interior space containing enzymes for respiration

questions.explanation: The matrix is the fluid-filled space inside the inner membrane of the mitochondrion. It contains enzymes for the Krebs cycle, as well as mitochondrial DNA and ribosomes.

questions.stem: Why do mitochondria have their own DNA?

options.text: It supports the endosymbiotic theory - that mitochondria were once independent organisms

questions.explanation: Mitochondria contain their own circular DNA and ribosomes, supporting the endosymbiotic theory that they evolved from ancient prokaryotic organisms that were engulfed by larger cells.

questions.stem: Which types of cells would have the most mitochondria?

options.text: Cells with high energy demands, such as muscle cells, nerve cells, and sperm cells
Cells that do not need energy

questions.explanation: Cells with high energy requirements have many mitochondria. Muscle cells need energy for contraction, nerve cells for transmitting impulses, and sperm cells for swimming.

questions.stem: What is the approximate size of a mitochondrion?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are typically 1-10 micrometres long, similar in size to bacteria. They can be seen with a light microscope but their internal structure is best observed with an electron microscope.

questions.stem: How does the structure of the inner mitochondrial membrane relate to its function?

options.text: It is smooth to allow fast movement
It is permeable to all substances
It is folded into cristae to increase surface area for ATP-producing reactions

questions.explanation: The inner membrane is highly folded into cristae, providing a large surface area for the electron transport chain and ATP synthase enzymes. This maximises the rate of ATP production during aerobic respiration.
